content: Your doctor has prescribed an intravenous hydration solution for injection. This treatment is intended for patients who are unable or advised not to consume fluids orally through drinking or eating. The hydration solution will be administered via a needle or catheter inserted into your vein, typically over a period of 10 to 12 hours each day, or as directed by your physician. The hydration solution may contain a combination of sugar and carbohydrates to provide energy, as well as electrolytes and trace elements. The specific composition of your solution will depend on your medical condition and needs. Electrolytes may include sodium, potassium, chloride, phosphate, calcium, and magnesium, while trace elements may include zinc, copper, manganese, and chromium. These components are essential for the proper functioning of nearly every organ in your body. They support the normal operation of your heart, muscles, and nerves, and help prevent dehydration. This medication may also be prescribed for other purposes. If you have questions about its use, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Your healthcare provider may monitor the effectiveness of your treatment and any potential side effects through laboratory tests and physical examinations. It is crucial to attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and the laboratory. The duration of your treatment will depend on how your body responds to the medication. Precautions Before Administration: Inform your doctor and pharmacist if you have any allergies to medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially corticosteroids, heart or diabetes medications, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of diabetes, or any heart, kidney, liver, thyroid, or lung diseases. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while receiving hydration therapy, contact your doctor immediately. Administering Your Medication: Before using the hydration solution, inspect it carefully. The solution should be clear and free of any floating particles. Gently squeeze the bag or examine the container to ensure there are no leaks. Do not use the solution if it appears discolored, contains particles, or if the bag or container is damaged. Use a new solution and show the damaged one to your healthcare provider. It is essential to follow your healthcare provider’s instructions precisely when using this medication. Do not alter your dosing schedule without consulting your provider. If you encounter a mechanical issue, such as a blockage in the tubing, needle, or catheter, your provider may advise you to stop the infusion. If this occurs, contact your healthcare provider immediately to ensure your therapy can continue without interruption. Side Effects: Hydration therapy may cause side effects. Contact your healthcare provider immediately if you experience any of the following symptoms: Fever or chills Stomach pain Difficulty breathing Rapid weight gain or loss Increased urination Upset stomach or vomiting Confusion or memory loss Muscle weakness, twitching, or cramps Swelling of the hands, feet, or legs Increased thirst Tingling in the hands or feet Overactive reflexes Seizures If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Storing Your Medication: Your healthcare provider will likely supply you with several days’ worth of hydration solution at a time. You will be instructed to store it in the refrigerator or freezer. Before using your next dose, remove it from the refrigerator 4 to 6 hours in advance and place it in a clean, dry area to allow it to reach room temperature. If additional hydration is stored in the freezer, transfer a 24-hour supply to the refrigerator for the next day’s use. Do not refreeze the medication. Store your medication exactly as directed, and ensure you understand the proper storage requirements. Keep your supplies in a clean, dry place when not in use, and store all medications and supplies out of the reach of children. Your healthcare provider will instruct you on how to safely dispose of used needles, syringes, tubing, and containers to prevent accidental injury. In Case of Emergency or Overdose: If an overdose occurs, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Signs of Infection: If you are receiving hydration therapy through a vein or under the skin, it is important to recognize the symptoms of a catheter-related infection. This type of infection occurs at the site where the needle enters your vein or skin.
